authority_compensation_policy.2023: The 2023 final-key PDFs mark 16 cells “To be Compensated” across eight booklets. The in-force 2020 Rules establish 200 marks per paper / 2 hours (Rule 9(1)(b)) and one-third penalty for wrong or multiple answers, no penalty for blank (Schedule I A.2–5); they do not state who receives marks for dropped questions. The 2024 consolidated scheme says dropped-question marks are awarded to all candidates, but its notice says it takes effect immediately on 2024-02-01; do not project this later rule backward to the June 2023 exam. No direct 2023 source found resolves attempt-dependence or penalty interaction. Keep 2023 compensation scoring blocked pending year-specific authority evidence.
authority_compensation_policy.2025: MPSC scheme notification No. A.12034/18/2025-MPSC(EXAM), dated 2025-08-01 (official MPSC PDF, SHA256 0e8af2c954ee6f9a8fa1283d05b35148c264acbf58427ee2a6034e2b39eaff25) states: if any answer key is successfully challenged, corresponding mark(s) shall be compensated to all candidates. The scheme gives 2 hours, 200 marks, 100 questions × 2 marks, one-third wrong-answer penalty, 33% Paper-II qualification. This resolves attempt eligibility: all candidates, irrespective of attempt. The separate 2025 Rules also treat multiple marked responses as wrong and blank as no penalty. Still unresolved from inspected authority text: whether a wrong/multiple response to a compensated item also incurs the ordinary penalty or the item is scored as a flat compensation outcome. Confirm before coding that interaction.
